python3 << 'EOF'
import math
import statistics

# National Defense expenditures (in millions) for fiscal years 1933-1941
expenditures = {
    1933: 680,
    1934: 531,
    1935: 689,
    1936: 900,
    1937: 929,
    1938: 1029,
    1939: 1206,
    1940: 1657,
    1941: 6301
}

# Calculate year-to-year log growth rates
log_growth_rates = []
years = sorted(expenditures.keys())

for i in range(1, len(years)):
    prev_year = years[i-1]
    curr_year = years[i]
    prev_exp = expenditures[prev_year]
    curr_exp = expenditures[curr_year]
    
    # Calculate log growth rate: ln(E(t) / E(t-1))
    growth_rate = math.log(curr_exp / prev_exp)
    log_growth_rates.append(growth_rate)
    print(f"{prev_year}->{curr_year}: {prev_exp} -> {curr_exp}, log growth = {growth_rate:.6f}")

print(f"\nLog growth rates: {log_growth_rates}")

# Calculate mean and population standard deviation
mean = statistics.mean(log_growth_rates)
# Using population standard deviation (ddof=0)
std_dev = statistics.pstdev(log_growth_rates)

print(f"\nMean: {mean:.6f}")
print(f"Population Standard Deviation: {std_dev:.6f}")

# Coefficient of variation = std_dev / mean
# But since we're looking at volatility index, it might be just the std_dev
# Let me check: CV = std/mean
cv = std_dev / mean

print(f"Coefficient of Variation (std/mean): {cv:.6f}")
print(f"\nVolatility Index (CV): {cv:.2f}")
EOF

import math
import statistics

# National Defense expenditures (in millions) for fiscal years 1933-1941
expenditures = {
    1933: 680,
    1934: 531,
    1935: 689,
    1936: 900,
    1937: 929,
    1938: 1029,
    1939: 1206,
    1940: 1657,
    1941: 6301
}

# Calculate year-to-year log growth rates
log_growth_rates = []
years = sorted(expenditures.keys())

for i in range(1, len(years)):
    prev_year = years[i-1]
    curr_year = years[i]
    prev_exp = expenditures[prev_year]
    curr_exp = expenditures[curr_year]
    
    # Calculate log growth rate: ln(E(t) / E(t-1))
    growth_rate = math.log(curr_exp / prev_exp)
    log_growth_rates.append(growth_rate)

# Using population standard deviation
mean = statistics.mean(log_growth_rates)
std_dev = statistics.pstdev(log_growth_rates)

# Coefficient of variation = std / mean (absolute value to handle negative mean case)
cv = std_dev / abs(mean)

print(f"Log growth rates: {log_growth_rates}")
print(f"Mean: {mean:.6f}")
print(f"Population Standard Deviation: {std_dev:.6f}")
print(f"Coefficient of Variation (std/|mean|): {cv:.6f}")
print(f"\nRounded to nearest hundredth: {cv:.2f}")

# Also show just standard deviation as alternative interpretation
print(f"\n--- Alternative: just std dev ---")
print(f"Population std dev (volatility): {std_dev:.6f}")
print(f"Rounded: {std_dev:.2f}")

import math

    1934: 531,
    1935: 689,

    1940: 1657,
    1941: 6301
}

print("=== Expenditure Volatility Index Calculation ===")
print("Years: 1933-1941 (fiscal years)")
print("Expenditures (millions of dollars):")
for year, exp in expenditures.items():
    print(f"  {year}: {exp}")
print()

# Calculate year-to-year log growth rates: ln(E(t) / E(t-1))
log_growth_rates = []
years = sorted(expenditures.keys())

print("Year-to-year log growth rates:")
for i in range(1, len(years)):
    prev_year = years[i-1]
    curr_year = years[i]
    prev_exp = expenditures[prev_year]
    curr_exp = expenditures[curr_year]
    
    growth_rate = math.log(curr_exp / prev_exp)
    log_growth_rates.append(growth_rate)
    print(f"  {prev_year}->{curr_year}: ln({curr_exp}/{prev_exp}) = {growth_rate:.6f}")

print()

# Population standard deviation (the question specifies "use population standard deviation where relevant")
mean = statistics.mean(log_growth_rates)
std_dev = statistics.pstdev(log_growth_rates)  # population std dev (ddof=0)

# Coefficient of variation = std_dev / mean
cv = std_dev / mean

print(f"Mean of log growth rates: {mean:.6f}")
print(f"Population standard deviation: {std_dev:.6f}")
print(f"Coefficient of Variation (volatility index): {std_dev}/{mean:.4f} = {cv:.6f}")
print()
print(f"FINAL ANSWER (rounded to nearest hundredth): {cv:.2f}")
